lesson_title: The Chalk Line: Accrued and Prepaid, Made Obvious
hook_text: Money in your hand that ISN'T yours yet. Accounting's strangest truth.
clip_script: Draw a chalk line on the floor: midnight, last day of June. Everything the shop earned and used on this side belongs to this year's report card. Everything past it — next year's. Simple. Except money refuses to respect the line. June's electricity gets billed in JULY — but the heaters ran in June. A year of insurance paid in March — two-thirds of it protects NEXT year. A tenant pays a month ahead — and here's the strangest one: that money, sitting in your hand, is a DEBT. You hold the cash; the tenant holds the claim to a month you haven't delivered. Four corners, two questions: whose year does it belong to, and has the cash moved? Put every amount where the USING happened — and let the balance sheet keep the sticky notes and the parcels.
visual_style: A glowing chalk line across a dark floor; coins and bills hopping back and forth across it; sticky notes and small wrapped parcels accumulating on a shelf labelled Balance Sheet.
mood: Mind-bending but friendly — the aha of money-in-hand-as-debt.
pacing: Quick scene-setting, three escalating examples, landing on the money-as-debt twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort all four corners yourself.
